extraction.name: CADS-dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale collection of 22,022 CT volumes with full annotations for 167 anatomical structures, establishing the most extensive whole-body CT dataset to date for whole-body CT segmentation.
extraction.license: Mixed (Users must comply with individual licenses and terms of use for each source dataset, including CC BY 4.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, etc.)
extraction.creator: Murong Xu, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Fernando Navarro, et al.
extraction.citeAs: Xu, M., Amiranashvili, T., Navarro, F., et al. CADS : A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography. arXiv:2507.22953v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Aggregation of 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources including public archives (e.g., TCIA, medical challenges), hospital cohorts, 484 newly acquired head CTs, and 586 newly released triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 21% of images contain partial annotations from public sources; 79% lack any annotations initially. Existing datasets often miss costovertebral joints in rib annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CT volumes from over 100 medical centers across 16 countries, including TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K, VISCERAL, KiTS, LiTS, and newly acquired head/abdominal scans.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Gaussian filter (σ=5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) applied to facial regions for privacy anonymization in newly acquired hospital head CT scans.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reorientation to standard RAS convention; resampling to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution; simplification of affine transformation matrices (removing rotation/translation); intensity scaling from 5th to 95th percentiles to [0,1] with clipping.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-stage process: 1) Specialized models trained on high-quality annotations generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled scans. 2) Shape-informed quality control using neural implicit functions filters unreliable pseudo-labels. 3) Multi-strategy label generation (GT-flavor, Pseudo-flavor, Shape-flavor) with statistical ranking to select best labels. 4) Manual annotations by medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist for specific structures (OARs). 5) Progressive merging of labels prioritizing reliability.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Statistical ranking of model flavors using Dice and HD95 metrics on in-distribution and out-of-distribution data; significance testing (p<0.05); progressive merging order based on label reliability; manual review and curation of test set annotations to correct systematic errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist (JCP).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net, Neural implicit functions (auto-decoder), vesselFM, ANTS non-rigid transformation, TPTBox Python library.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Publicly available via Hugging Face. No specific versioning or maintenance plan mentioned.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Advances robust AI solutions in radiology; makes comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible; streamlines treatment planning in radiation oncology; enables automated organ volume quantification and large-scale population studies.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential elimination of pathological cases with atypical anatomical variations due to shape-based quality assessment exclusion strategy; limited training data for certain structures (e.g., buccal mucosa); systematic errors in existing public datasets (e.g., ribs, vertebrae) propagated if not corrected.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Excludes hands and feet; brain mask may be too inclusive; optic chiasm under-segmented; heart segmentation omits superior portions; rectum appears short; trachea limited to air content; facial features anonymized limiting facial analysis; exclusion strategy may remove valuable pathological edge cases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. Specific uses: Whole-body CT segmentation, radiation therapy planning, anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration, anatomy-guided synthesis, longitudinal organ tracking, personalized anatomical modeling, large-scale population studies.
